children.text: Waves and phase transitions in spin systems

Treat spin vectors classically except for E=ℏω,p=ℏk in the quasiparticle interpretation. A rotating uniform ring has positive charge Q,mass M,radius R and magnetic moment μ=γL. In A3 the separation d≫R is perpendicular to the ring moments as in the diagram. In B a long chain of fixed spin vectors of magnitude S lies along x at spacing a, with energy \(E=-J\sum_i\mathbf S_i\cdot\mathbf S_{i+1}\), J>0. Only nearest neighbours interact. For weak waves use Siz≈S and Ṡiz≈0. In C each spin is restricted to si=±1 along z and \(E=-\tilde J\sum_i s_is_{i+1}-h\sum_i s_i\), with N≫1, J̃≥0 and temperature T. Ignore edges. The source's prescribed one-neighbour energy-replacement approximation in C4-C7 sets J̃eff=J̃s̄. This exercise approximation differs from the usual two-neighbour local-field mean-field model. Neither approximation is the exact thermodynamics of a one-dimensional short-range Ising chain, which has no nonzero-temperature ordered phase.

a.2. Signed Larmor frequency

children.text: Waves and phase transitions in spin systems
Torque is \(\dot{\mathbf L}=\gamma\mathbf L\times\mathbf B\). Compare with \(\dot{\mathbf L}=\omega_L\hat z\times\mathbf L\), giving \(\omega_L=-\gamma B\).
The equatorial field of ring 1 is \(\mathbf B_1=-\mu_0\boldsymbol\mu_1/(4\pi d^3)\). Thus U=−μ2·B1 gives \(J_0=\mu_0\gamma^2/(4\pi d^3)\), positive.
The terms containing Si are \(-J\mathbf S_i\cdot(\mathbf S_{i-1}+\mathbf S_{i+1})\). Comparing with −γSi·Bi,eff gives \(\mathbf B_{i,eff}=(J/\gamma)(\mathbf S_{i-1}+\mathbf S_{i+1})\).
Apply magnetic torque: \[\frac{d\mathbf S_i}{dt}=J\mathbf S_i\times(\mathbf S_{i-1}+\mathbf S_{i+1}).\] Each spin keeps constant magnitude because its derivative is perpendicular to itself.

Linearization gives \(\dot S_{ix}=JS(2S_{iy}-S_{i-1,y}-S_{i+1,y})\) and \(\dot S_{iy}=-JS(2S_{ix}-S_{i-1,x}-S_{i+1,x})\). Take equal-amplitude quadrature waves Sx=δScos(kai−ωt), Sy=δSsin(kai−ωt). Then \[\omega=2JS[1-\cos(ka)].\] The opposite phase convention can reverse signed frequency. The field checks its positive branch.
\(\omega\simeq JSa^2k^2\). With E=ℏω,p=ℏk, compare E=(JSa²/ℏ)p² with p²/(2meff), giving \(m_{eff}=\hbar/(2JSa^2)\).

The spin wave has no y momentum, so pin cosθin=pout cosθout. Its x momentum is ps=pin sinθin−pout sinθout and energy Es=(pin²−pout²)/(2mn). Thus \[m_{eff}=m_n\frac{\sin^2(\theta_{in}-\theta_{out})}{\cos^2\theta_{out}-\cos^2\theta_{in}}=m_n\frac{\sin(\theta_{in}-\theta_{out})}{\sin(\theta_{in}+\theta_{out})}.\] Choose physical angles giving positive energy loss and mass. If angles are instead measured from the chain, convert them before using this expression.
The ±z states have energies −h and +h. Boltzmann weights give \(p_\uparrow/p_\downarrow=e^{2h/(k_BT)}\). For negative h the labels remain ±z, so up is then anti-aligned with the field.

Normalize the two Boltzmann weights to obtain \(\bar s=p_\uparrow-p_\downarrow=\tanh[h/(k_BT)]\). All curves are odd through the origin. For a large field range they saturate near ±1, for a small range they are nearly linear with slope 1/(kBT), and the intermediate range gives a smooth unsaturated S-shaped curve.
All spins align, with either global sign, so every bond contributes −J̃. For an open chain Eg=−J̃(N−1)≈−J̃N. A periodic chain has exactly N bonds.

The explicitly prescribed replacement gives \(\tilde J_{eff}=\tilde J\bar s\). This matches the official scheme's single-counted energy ansatz. For comparison, a thermodynamically consistent local-field decoupling uses both neighbours, field 2J̃s̄ and an additive correction NJ̃s̄². Those are different approximations, so the next items use the one requested here.

For the source ansatz, \(\bar s=\tanh[\tilde J\bar s/(k_BT)]\). The zero solution always exists. Nonzero roots appear when the right-hand slope at zero exceeds one, giving \(T_c=\tilde J/k_B\). Above Tc only zero exists, below Tc there are also two opposite roots. This is the transition of the stated approximation, not an exact 1D transition.

Expand tanh x≈x−x³/3. The roots are \(\bar s=0\) and \(\bar s\simeq\pm\sqrt{3(T_c-T)/T_c}\). Keeping cubic-order temperature factors gives ±√[3(T/Tc)²(1−T/Tc)]. Draw the full roots from the implicit equation, not the near-critical expansion down to T=0: nonzero branches approach ±1 with zero slope at zero temperature and merge with vertical tangents at Tc. The zero branch persists below Tc but is unstable in the mean-field picture.
c.7. Magnetic phases in the approximation

The approximate model is paramagnetic above Tc and ferromagnetic below Tc, where it supports spontaneous nonzero s̄. The exact infinite one-dimensional short-range chain orders only at zero temperature.

solution.text:
Waves and phase transitions in spin systems
a.1. Ring gyromagnetic ratio
\(L=MR^2\omega\) and \(\mu=Q\omega R^2/2\), hence \(\gamma=Q/(2M)\).
a.2. Signed Larmor frequency
Torque is \(\dot{\mathbf L}=\gamma\mathbf L\times\mathbf B\). Compare with \(\dot{\mathbf L}=\omega_L\hat z\times\mathbf L\), giving \(\omega_L=-\gamma B\).
a.3. Dipole coupling energy

The terms containing Si are \(-J\mathbf S_i\cdot(\mathbf S_{i-1}+\mathbf S_{i+1})\). Comparing with −γSi·Bi,eff gives \(\mathbf B_{i,eff}=(J/\gamma)(\mathbf S_{i-1}+\mathbf S_{i+1})\).
b.2. Spin evolution
Apply magnetic torque: \[\frac{d\mathbf S_i}{dt}=J\mathbf S_i\times(\mathbf S_{i-1}+\mathbf S_{i+1}).\] Each spin keeps constant magnitude because its derivative is perpendicular to itself.

b.5. Neutron-scattering mass

Thus \[m_{eff}=m_n\frac{\sin^2(\theta_{in}-\theta_{out})}{\cos^2\theta_{out}-\cos^2\theta_{in}}=m_n\frac{\sin(\theta_{in}-\theta_{out})}{\sin(\theta_{in}+\theta_{out})}.\] Choose physical angles giving positive energy loss and mass. c.1. Independent-spin probability ratio
The ±z states have energies −h and +h. Boltzmann weights give \(p_\uparrow/p_\downarrow=e^{2h/(k_BT)}\). For negative h the labels remain ±z, so up is then anti-aligned with the field.
c.2. Polarization curve

For a large field range they saturate near ±1, for a small range they are nearly linear with slope 1/(kBT), and the intermediate range gives a smooth unsaturated S-shaped curve.
c.3. Ground-state energy
All spins align, with either global sign, so every bond contributes −J̃. For an open chain Eg=−J̃(N−1)≈−J̃N. A periodic chain has exactly N bonds.
c.4. Prescribed average-energy replacement
The explicitly prescribed replacement gives \(\tilde J_{eff}=\tilde J\bar s\). This matches the official scheme's single-counted energy ansatz. For comparison, a thermodynamically consistent local-field decoupling uses both neighbours, field 2J̃s̄ and an additive correction NJ̃s̄². Those are different approximations, so the next items use the one requested here.
c.5. Self-consistency and critical temperature
For the source ansatz, \(\bar s=\tanh[\tilde J\bar s/(k_BT)]\). The zero solution always exists. Nonzero roots appear when the right-hand slope at zero exceeds one, giving \(T_c=\tilde J/k_B\). Above Tc only zero exists, below Tc there are also two opposite roots. This is the transition of the stated approximation, not an exact 1D transition.
c.6. Near-critical branches
Expand tanh x≈x−x³/3. The roots are \(\bar s=0\) and \(\bar s\simeq\pm\sqrt{3(T_c-T)/T_c}\). Keeping cubic-order temperature factors gives ±√[3(T/Tc)²(1−T/Tc)]. The zero branch persists below Tc but is unstable in the mean-field picture.
